# Owen Ford

## Overview

- **Age:** About 30 or 35 years old  <sub>[v4 c24 P6](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0006)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019)</sub>
- **Status:** Alive  <sub>[v5 c2 P67](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0067)</sub>
- **Origin:** Ontario  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019)</sub>
- **Role:** Newspaper man and author / novelist  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019), [v4 c24 P6](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0006), [v5 c2 P67](../source/v05-c02.md#nw-v05-c02-p0067)</sub>

## Appearance

Owen is a very handsome, tall, and broad-shouldered man with thick brown hair, a finely-cut nose and chin, and large, brilliant dark-gray eyes. He has nice-shaped ears and a friendly smile that reveals nice teeth. While his unsmiling expression can appear sad and absent, mirth and humor light up his face when he smiles.

_Sources: [v4 c23 P8](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0008), [v4 c23 P9](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0009), [v4 c23 P10](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0010), [v4 c24 P6](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0006)_

## Personality

Owen possesses a charming, likeable, and warm personality with a delightful voice and smile. He is deeply artistic and passionate, possessing a strong sense of humor, vivid imagination, and the ability to express himself eloquently. He is honorable and considerate, refusing to reveal his feelings to a woman who is not free, even while suffering intense personal heartbreak.

_Sources: [v4 c23 P10](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0010), [v4 c24 P6](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0006), [v4 c24 P7](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0007), [v4 c25 P13](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0013), [v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002), [v4 c26 P5](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0005)_

## History

After recovering from a severe bout of typhoid, Owen Ford traveled to Four Winds to regain his health by the sea and visit the place where his grandparents had lived. While staying with Leslie Moore, he met Captain Jim Boyd and was inspired to write a book based on the old sea captain's life-book. During his summer at Four Winds, he fell deeply in love with Leslie, but maintained his silence out of respect for her marital status before returning to Toronto. After Leslie was freed from her tragic circumstances, Owen returned to Four Winds the following summer and proposed to her in the garden of the little house. The two were married at Christmas and went on to have two children, Kenneth and Persis. He published a successful novel based on Captain Jim's life and later bought the old House of Dreams to serve as a summer vacation home for his family.

_Sources: [v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019), [v4 c23 P34](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0034), [v4 c24 P31](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0031), [v4 c25 P0](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0000), [v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002), [v4 c27 P0](../source/v04-c27.md#nw-v04-c27-p0000), [v4 c34 P30](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0030), [v4 c38 P9](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0009), [v4 c38 P10](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0010), [v4 c39 P5](../source/v04-c39.md#nw-v04-c39-p0005), [v4 c40 P11](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0011), [v4 c40 P56](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0056), [v5 c4 P54](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0054), [v5 c4 P56](../source/v05-c04.md#nw-v05-c04-p0056)_

## Background by volume

- Grandson of John Selwyn, the schoolmaster who built the house in Four Winds  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019)</sub>
- Son of John Selwyn's eldest daughter, Alice  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019), [v4 c24 P22](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0022)</sub>
- Suffered a bad spell of typhoid fever prior to coming to Four Winds  <sub>[v4 c22 P19](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0019)</sub>

## Quotes

> Mrs. Blythe, this is a wonderful book—absolutely wonderful. If I could take it and use the material for a book I feel certain I could make the novel of the year out of it. Do you suppose Captain Jim would let me do it?  <sub>[v4 c25 P0](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0000)</sub>

> Mrs. Blythe, I love Leslie. LOVE her! That seems too weak a word!  <sub>[v4 c26 P2](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0002)</sub>

> Perhaps, it is the prisoned infinite in us calling out to its kindred infinite as expressed in that visible perfection.  <sub>[v4 c26 P24](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0024)</sub>

> Yes—love triumphant and perfect. Leslie, you know—you understand. I have loved you from the first. And I KNOW you love me—I don’t need to ask you. But I want to hear you say it—my darling—my darling!  <sub>[v4 c38 P9](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0009)</sub>
